subject: Implementation fee restructure / labor-rate change request
messages:
From: Ethan Young <eyoung@bluewave.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura McIntyre <laura.mcintyre@bluewave.ai>, Ben Ross <bross@bluewave.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: SOW change: implementation phasing + labor rate cap

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the platform looks really promising. Our leadership asked us to revisit the implementation fee structure and a couple of scope items before we execute the order form. Two asks:  

1) Can we move the implementation labor from a time-and-materials line to a not-to-exceed (NTE) labor cap? We want more predictability on the professional services spend during ramp.
2) We need a shorter onboarding phase for the streaming ingestion piece — move from 8 weeks to 5 weeks and include a deployment hardening checklist in the SOW.

I've attached a marked-up SOW (BlueWave_SOW_markup_v1.docx) with comments. From a commercial POV, we are open to a small increase to the committed capacity in exchange for the NTE labor cap, but we'll need the updated order form reflecting the change.

Can you loop in legal and procurement on your side and share a proposed change order? Also please include an estimate for the NTE labor cap and any impact to timing.

Appreciate it —
Ethan
Ethan Young
Director, Platform Engineering
BlueWave Therapeutics

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW change: implementation phasing + labor rate cap

Ethan —

Thanks for the clear notes and the annotated SOW. We can definitely support an NTE labor cap model; want to make sure legal signs off on the exact language and the contingency for out-of-scope items. I'll draft a change order and an updated SOW showing the shortened onboarding milestones and a deployment hardening checklist.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll draft the change order (CO) that converts implementation labor to an NTE line item and shows the alternate capacity tier we discussed as trade consideration.
- Looping in our sales lead Karthik and legal (cc'd internally) to review redlines and the specific clause for "out-of-scope" / change-control.
- Expect a first draft by EOD Tues (20 Jul).

If BlueWave is comfortable with a modest capacity increase (we'll propose two options), we can keep the overall contract term and the current SLA intact.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BlueWave CO draft — legal review items and commercial options

Laura / Karthik —

Looping you both in on BlueWave's request to convert implementation labor to an NTE cap and shorten the onboarding from 8 -> 5 weeks. I drafted a CO and a redlined SOW (attached) with two commercial options. Quick read below, then please advise on the legal language and commercial preference.

Summary of proposed CO (high level):
- Option A (conservative): NTE labor cap = $95,000 (covers stated onboarding scope). Customer keeps current committed capacity.
- Option B (trade): NTE labor cap = $75,000 if customer increases committed throughput by 20% for the 12-month term.
- Implementation schedule: onboarding milestones compressed to 5 weeks; added deployment hardening checklist as Exhibit A to SOW.
- Change-control: any additional work outside the SOW to be tracked via written Change Request; work will be billed at our standard PS rates beyond the NTE.

Legal questions / asks for Laura:
1) Can we phrase the NTE clause so that it is a flat cap for the listed onboarding tasks but explicitly excludes customer-caused delays (we should preserve carve-outs).
2) For Option B, we want a simple order-form amendment tied to capacity. Is there any regulatory wording we need for the US healthcare customer (PII/PHI handling) that would change the labor billing or on-site requirements?
3) Any concerns about rollback or termination rights triggered by a failed onboarding within 5 weeks?

Karthik: can you confirm the two commercial options look reasonable and that we can provide the resource commitment to meet the 5-week timeline if BlueWave signs quickly? Also include any thoughts on discounting cadence for committed throughput.

Attachments: CW-BlueWave_CO_v2.docx; SOW_Implementation_Redline.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SOW change: implementation phasing + labor rate cap

Ethan —

Appreciate the patience while we reviewed this internally. Attached are two files: a clean change order (CW-BlueWave_CO_v2.docx) and a redlined SOW showing the 5-week onboarding schedule and the new "Deployment Hardening Checklist" (SOW_Implementation_Redline.pdf). Key points: 

- We included both Option A (NTE $95k) and Option B (NTE $75k + 20% committed throughput uplift) in the change order so you have a clear trade-off.
- Legal asked for one small clarification in the NTE language: carve out customer-caused delays and third-party integration delays from the cap. We added explicit call-outs and a short change-control flow.
- No change to the term or SLAs.

If the trade (Option B) looks attractive, we can generate the amended order form reflecting the new committed throughput and send a DocuSign request. Otherwise, sign Option A as-is. Either way, once signed we will schedule the onboarding kickoff within 5 business days.

DocuSign (if you'd like to sign electronically): https://www.docusign.com/recipient/placeholder/link/abc123

Next steps for BlueWave: please confirm which option you prefer and who will sign on your side. Our legal contact (Laura Bennett) is copied if you want to take a last pass on the redline language.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Marissa Cole
